summary.headline: Dodla Dairy Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% to INR1,196 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.4% as milk procurement costs outran price hikes.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.4% YoY to INR1,196 crore, with EBITDA of INR64.1 crore (5.4% margin) and PAT of INR36.6 crore (3.1% margin). Milk procurement cost rose to INR43.2/litre from INR37.3 a year ago, while the INR2.5/litre price hike taken late in the quarter (mostly September) only partly offset it, so the milk spread narrowed to INR18.7/litre from INR20. Africa was the standout at INR179 crore (+56%). Management guided to a return to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin for Oct-Dec quarter and H2 on current price levels, with procurement prices expected to stay flat.

segments.name: India dairy (milk and VAP)
segments.commentary: Milk procurement 21.3 lakh litres/day (+9.3% YoY); milk sales volume 14.2 lakh litres/day (+8.4%); milk sales realisation INR61.9/litre vs INR57.3 a year ago. Curd and curd-based products volume +23% YoY to 444.7 MT/day.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue INR179 crore (+56% YoY), driven by a 68.5% rise in milk sales. Greenfield plant in Uganda on 70 acres; civil work started about a month before the call, with operations targeted for FY28 beginning.

segments.name: OSAM (Bihar/Jharkhand)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR82.37 crore at 1.33 lakh litres/day. EBITDA margin 1% in Q2 vs 2.6% in Q1; management is prioritising operational stabilisation over margin and expects 4-5% EBITDA from Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Orgafeed (cattle feed)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 40% YoY in Q2 FY27, but margins hit as raw material costs could not be fully passed on to farmers.

segments.name: Curd (within VAP)
segments.commentary: Realisation INR59.15/litre vs INR56.16 a year ago; EBITDA margin about 12%, gross margin about 19%. Buttermilk and lassi margins 20-23%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to return to about 7.5-8% for Oct-Dec quarter and H2 FY27 at current price levels, assuming no further procurement inflation.
Full impact of the INR2.5/litre price hike to show in Q3 FY27; further hikes possible if cooperatives implement announced larger increases.
Management expects milk procurement prices to stay flat through Q3 and Q4 FY27 (only INR0.20-0.30 locational variation noted).
Maharashtra plant: liquid milk operations from March-April 2027; powder operations from September 2027.
Capex total: earlier INR600 crore estimate (Maharashtra INR280 crore, Africa INR60-70 crore, OSAM net acquisition) may rise 5-10% on inflation; a further feed plant decision is 3-6 months away.
India revenue for H2 FY27 guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, versus management's earlier figure of INR1,300-1,400 crore.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR66 crore, mainly Maharashtra expansion; cash and bank balance INR659.4 crore as of September 2026.
Africa greenfield (Uganda) on 70 acres, targeting operations from FY28; Kenya focus on market penetration and own procurement network.
Feed capacity at about 6,000-7,000 tonnes installed, utilisable 8,000-9,000 tonnes; another feed plant for Maharashtra under consideration.
Maharashtra (Itkal) plant: liquid milk from March-April 2027, powder from September 2027.
H1 FY27 inventory build of INR76 crore (SMP and butter); inventory stood at INR232 crore at September 2026.
demand_pricing: Milk procurement cost INR43.2/litre in Q2 FY27 vs INR41 in Q1 and INR37.3 in Q2 FY26; management says the cost has peaked and was front-loaded into Q1-Q2 given unusually early price rises.
Procurement by state (lakh litres/day): Andhra Pradesh 4.76, Karnataka 5.1, Maharashtra 2.99, Tamil Nadu 4.25, Telangana 0.45.
Q1 to Q2 price-cost gap: realisation +INR1.99/litre vs procurement +INR2.93/litre sequentially; YoY realisation +INR3.3 vs procurement +INR4.84.
Consolidated realisation INR65.06/litre (vs INR62.53); India INR63.59 (vs INR63.07); overseas INR73.14 (vs INR60.11); HR Foods INR67.05 (vs INR63.36); consolidated VAP realisation INR66.46.
VAP mix in INR327 crore: curd and curd products INR251 crore, paneer INR21 crore, ghee and butter INR22.1 crore, ice cream INR11 crore, flavoured milk INR13 crore, sweets INR6.6 crore.
Packing material costs +41.6% YoY; overhead cost per litre up on inflation and geopolitical factors.
OSAM competition: Sudha (about 70% share, with late payments), ITC, Amul, and UP brands Gyan Dairy and Namaste India are entering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for milk procurement cost and pricing, and what margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes procurement prices stay at elevated levels with no dip. The Sept price hike flows through in full from Q3, and Dodla should return to 7.5-8% EBITDA for Oct-Dec and H2 at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 seasonal procurement inflation recur?
qa_highlights.answer: B.V.K. Reddy said Q1 and Q2 prices were already elevated, that no Q3 or Q4 hike is seen, and that rains in southern coastal areas have improved availability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Meadow India JV and what does it cover?
qa_highlights.answer: A 40:60 JV with Meadow India Holdings (UK-linked) to sell B2B dairy ingredients such as tailored skim milk powder and inclusions. Dodla invests INR1 crore for its 40% stake, and it is an exploratory venture.

qa_highlights.question: How will OSAM's low margin affect consolidated EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: OSAM revenue of INR250-300 crore at 4% EBITDA is about INR12 crore, so the drag is small (INR3-4 crore). India operations drive the margin recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Did the INR600 crore capex estimate change?
qa_highlights.answer: No material change. Capex may rise 5-10% on inflation. Maharashtra was earlier INR280 crore, Africa INR60-70 crore, and OSAM acquisition net of cash about INR600 crore in total.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the INR2.5/litre price hike holding and procurement prices staying flat through Q3-Q4; sustained cooperative hikes would be passed on with a lag.
Feed (concentrate) inflation expected as ethanol and CBG demand pulls maize; Orgafeed margins are under pressure.
OSAM stabilisation: own-procurement shift from agent model to direct farmer payment (25-30% done, target 70-80% by March); Sudha and new entrants competing.
El Nino and drought risk in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; buffalo milk supply declining year on year.
Maharashtra plant commissioning timelines (March-April 2027 liquid, September 2027 powder) and Uganda plant FY28 start.
Q2 deferred tax charge INR5.77 crore in H1 (CDDL first-time DTL, HR Food tax-rate change).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term margin recovery and the Africa growth story, but cautious on near-term profitability, which management attributes to the late price pass-through. Evasive on OSAM's margin path and the Sids Farm stake, where answers were brief. Some Q&A answers were loose (e.g. the India revenue run-rate), and the call was offered to be followed up offline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery depends on the INR2.5/litre hike holding and procurement staying flat; OSAM margin is 1% in Q2 (guided 4-5% from Q3), Orgafeed margins are squeezed by feed inflation, and El Nino/drought risk in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu is flagged.

rows.label: OSAM margin recovery to 4-5% EBITDA
rows.why: OSAM EBITDA margin fell to 1% in Q2 from 2.6% in Q1 on revenue of INR82.37 crore; management expects 4-5% from Q3 and Q4 as own-procurement moves from 25-30% toward 70-80% by March, but competition from Sudha, ITC and Amul is rising.

rows.label: Meadow India JV for B2B dairy ingredients
rows.why: A 40:60 JV with Meadow India Holdings for tailored SMP and inclusions needs only INR1 crore for Dodla's 40% stake, but it is exploratory with no revenue figure given.

rows.label: Africa growth momentum
rows.why: Africa revenue was a record INR179 crore (+56% YoY) on a 68.5% rise in milk sales, and the Kenya focus on own procurement is under way.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term margin recovery to 7.5-8% and on Africa growth, but cautious on near-term profit because price pass-through lagged procurement inflation, and it was brief on OSAM margins and the Sids Farm stake.
